topics.label: Course and Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Origins of Cancer and Determinants of Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer development by examining the relative contributions of intrinsic cellular processes, environmental exposures, and genetic predisposition.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote oncogenesis, highlighted by the cooperative mechanism between viral infection and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how chemical and physical mutagens undergo metabolic processing in host tissues to induce DNA damage and transversion mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promotional factors, inflammatory microenvironments, and the developmental stage of host tissues facilitate tumor formation.

topics.label: Methods for Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the observational techniques and experimental assay systems used to detect and prove the carcinogenic potential of environmental agents.

topics.label: Risk-Benefit Balance and Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by evaluating how individuals and societies balance everyday environmental risks against practical benefits.
